pablodiazjorge-prompt-forge-template-cur.description: Reviews every lesson in knowledge/lessons/, merges duplicates, rejects unsafe or trivial ones, promotes lessons seen by several teammates into knowledge/memory/ or a team skill, retires stale or contradicted memory, and prepares the result as a pull request for human review. Use only when the user explicitly asks to "curate lessons", "organize knowledge", "promote lessons", or "run curate-lessons".
pablodiazjorge-prompt-forge-template-cur.author: pablodiazjorge

pablodiazjorge-prompt-forge-template-git.description: Non-interactive git usage and commit conventions for AI coding agents. Use when staging changes, committing, writing commit messages, naming branches, splitting work into pull requests, rebasing, or checking out a pull request in a worktree for review.
pablodiazjorge-prompt-forge-template-git.author: pablodiazjorge

pablodiazjorge-prompt-forge-template-pow.description: Pitfalls and safe patterns for running commands and writing scripts in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.x. Use when running terminal commands on Windows, writing or debugging .ps1 scripts, chaining commands, checking the exit code of a native executable, writing files that contain $ or template syntax, handling file encodings, or switching toolchain versions.
pablodiazjorge-prompt-forge-template-pow.author: pablodiazjorge

pablodiazjorge-prompt-forge-template-rec.description: Records a non-obvious failure, workaround, or project quirk as a lesson in knowledge/lessons/ so that teammates' agents do not repeat it. Use at a checkpoint (before committing, before opening a pull request, or when reporting a task as done) after something went wrong in a way another agent would likely repeat, after finding that an entry in knowledge/memory/ is wrong, or when the user says "record a lesson", "save this lesson", or "what did we learn".
pablodiazjorge-prompt-forge-template-rec.author: pablodiazjorge
